title: Saint Bernard, Abbot and Doctor of the Church
short_summary: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux, a Cistercian abbot and Doctor of the Church, is remembered for his reform of monastic life, his theological writing, and his preaching of devotion to Christ through Mary.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps his memorial on August 20.
He was born near Dijon, France, around 1090.
He entered the Cistercian monastery of Citeaux and founded the monastery of Clairvaux in 1115.
He is a Doctor of the Church, sometimes called the Mellifluous Doctor for the sweetness of his preaching.

sections.heading: Reformer of monastic life
sections.body: Bernard entered the young Cistercian reform and, still in his twenties, was sent to found the monastery of Clairvaux. Under his leadership Clairvaux became a center of disciplined, prayerful monastic life that spread widely across Europe.

sections.heading: Doctor of the Church
sections.body: Bernard's writings on Scripture, contemplative prayer, and the love of God shaped Western spirituality for centuries. The Church honors him as a Doctor for the depth and influence of his theological and spiritual teaching.

sections.heading: Preacher of devotion to Mary
sections.body: Bernard is closely associated with devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary, presenting her always in relation to Christ, as the one through whom the Church approaches her Son.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Contemplation ordered to charity
catholic_connection_sections.body: Bernard's teaching holds that contemplative love of God is meant to overflow into active charity, not remain a private experience apart from the life of the Church.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Marian devotion centered on Christ
catholic_connection_sections.body: His preaching on Mary consistently points back to Christ, showing that authentic Marian devotion draws the faithful closer to her Son rather than standing apart from him.
